Housing is not merely a policy priority, it is a maƩer of dignity, empowerment and social jusƟce. The Government of India is unwavering in its resolve to ensure that every family has a pucca roof over their heads. Guided by the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban was launched in 2015 with the historic commitment of achieving Housing for All. In the past decade, this resolve has translated into unprecedented outcomes. With over 97 lakh pucca houses completed and handed over to beneﬁciaries across the country, PMAY-U has not only built homes but also restored dignity, strengthened women's ownership, and empowered lakhs of urban poor families. By its sheer scale, transparency and speed of implementaƟon, PMAY-U stands today among the largest and most impacƞul urban housing programmes in the world. As India moves decisively on the path of rapid urbanisaƟon and economic transformaƟon, the aspiraƟons of our urban ciƟzens are rising. Recognising this, the Government launched PMAY-U 2.0 with the bold objecƟve of providing pucca houses to an addiƟonal one crore urban families, ensuring that the momentum of development leaves no one behind. The Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal under PMAY-U 2.0 represents our commitment to cooperaƟve and parƟcipatory development. It seeks to acƟvely mobilise the strengths of both public insƟtuƟons and private enterprises, encouraging proacƟve parƟcipaƟon and leveraging their experƟse, innovaƟon and resources to deliver aﬀordable housing at scale. This comprehensive guideline issued by the Ministry on AHP verƟcal of PMAY-U 2.0 will certainly provide a transparent, accountable and result-oriented framework for implementaƟon of AHP projects naƟonwide. I am conﬁdent that this guideline will further accelerate the pace of construcƟon and ensure Ɵmely delivery of quality houses to eligible urban beneﬁciaries. I call upon State Governments, Urban Local Bodies, public agencies and private developers to partner in this naƟonal mission with renewed dedicaƟon. Together, let us reaﬃrm our commitment to Housing for All, transforming aspiraƟons into reality, empowering families with security and dignity and strengthening the foundaƟon of inclusive and sustainable urban development as we march forward towards

Message Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban (PMAY-U), envisioned under the dynamic leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has empowered the poor and marginalized secƟons of society with a digniﬁed place to call home. By ensuring access to safe and aﬀordable housing, the Mission has not only transformed urban landscapes but also strengthened access to beƩer health, educaƟon and livelihood opportuniƟes. PMAY-U stands as a testament to our Government's unwavering commitment to Housing for All and inclusive, people-centric urban development that leaves no family behind. As we move forward into the next phase of PMAY-U 2.0 to address the addiƟonal demand of 1 crore urban households, our Government has once again demonstrated its ﬁrm belief in cooperaƟve federalism and outcome- driven governance. The Mission is implemented through diﬀerent verƟcals, among which Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) plays a pivotal role in leveraging both public and private sector parƟcipaƟon to accelerate housing delivery and ensure scale, speed, and transparency. This Standard OperaƟonal Guidelines clearly arƟculate the framework for implementaƟon of AHP through both public and private agencies. It deﬁnes the roles and responsibiliƟes of all stakeholders, streamline procedures for project applicaƟon and approval, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability at every stage. I believe that adopƟon of this guideline will further enhance the implementaƟon mechanism and bridge the gap between ciƟzens, implemenƟng agencies and Government insƟtuƟons in eﬀecƟve planning, implementaƟon and monitoring of AHP projects under PMAY-U 2.0 in a structured, transparent and outcome-oriented manner. With the collecƟve eﬀorts of all stakeholders, I am conﬁdent that PMAY-U 2.0 will play a transformaƟve role in shaping a stronger and more prosperous naƟon. Through this Mission, we reaﬃrm our resolve to build an inclusive and developed India, advancing steadily towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat. (Tokhan Sahu)

Urban India stands at a pivotal moment of transformaƟon expanding in scale, dynamism and opportunity. As our ciƟes grow, so does our collecƟve responsibility to ensure that this growth remains inclusive, equitable and sustainable. Access to safe, secure and aﬀordable housing is central to this vision, not only as a basic human necessity but also as a catalyst for economic acƟvity and social stability. The Government of India, under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, launched the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) to address the growing urban housing demand. The Mission has played a transformaƟve role by sancƟoning nearly 1.23 crore houses, of which more than 97 lakh have already been completed and delivered to eligible beneﬁciaries. Building upon this signiﬁcant progress, the Government in 2024 reaﬃrmed its commitment to achieving Housing for All through Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0). The renewed Mission aims to assist an addiƟonal one crore urban households, with a strengthened emphasis on convergence and alignment with State-level Aﬀordable Housing Policies and enhanced parƟcipaƟon of both public and private agencies. Under PMAY-U 2.0, the Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal serves as a criƟcal supply-side intervenƟon. It seeks to augment the stock of aﬀordable housing through structured collaboraƟon among Central and State Governments, Urban Local Bodies and private sector partners. By fostering partnerships and streamlining implementaƟon mechanisms, the AHP verƟcal is poised to accelerate delivery, improve quality standards and ensure that the beneﬁts of urban development reach every eligible household. To facilitate eﬀecƟve and transparent implementaƟon of the AHP verƟcal, a comprehensive guideline has been prepared which provides clear guidance on project conceptualisaƟon, appraisal, approval, execuƟon, monitoring and post-compleƟon processes. It deﬁnes the roles and responsibiliƟes of States/UTs, ULBs, implemenƟng agencies, and private developers, ensuring structured planning, accountability and Ɵmely delivery of housing projects across ciƟes with special emphasis on Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) principles. By insƟtuƟonalizing transparency, quality assurance and convergence with other urban missions, the document strengthens implementaƟon capacity and promotes full occupancy and long-term sustainability of AHP projects naƟonwide. With the collecƟve eﬀorts of Public and private sector agencies, PMAY-U 2.0 will conƟnue to shape ciƟes that are more liveable, connected and opportunity-driven. Foreword The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) laid a strong foundaƟon for addressing the housing needs of the urban poor by facilitaƟng the construcƟon and delivery of lakhs of pucca houses across the country. In the last decade, the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) supported the construcƟon of nearly 1.23 crore houses of which 97 lakh houses are complete and delivered to the beneﬁciaries. Building upon the signiﬁcant progress achieved, PMAY-U 2.0 represents a renewed and strengthened commitment to realizing the vision of Housing for All, with an enhanced focus on inclusion, sustainability and scale. Under PMAY- U 2.0, the Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal emerges as a key pillar, driving the creaƟon of quality housing stock by leveraging insƟtuƟonal capaciƟes, encouraging public and private collaboraƟon and harnessing private sector eﬃciencies to accelerate delivery and expand access to aﬀordable home ownership. To enable structured and impact driven implementaƟon of AHP projects, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Aﬀairs has prepared a comprehensive Standard OperaƟng Procedure (SoP) which provides detailed guidance on project conceptualisaƟon, appraisal, approval and execuƟon, while clearly deﬁning the roles and responsibiliƟes of all stakeholders. It seeks to streamline processes, enhance transparency and improve eﬃciency in project delivery. This document serves as a pracƟcal roadmap for implemenƟng agencies including private developers to translate policy into acƟon. The SoP also strengthens accountability through deﬁned Ɵmelines, digital monitoring mechanisms and convergence with State-level housing policies, thereby ensuring that projects are well formulated, ﬁnancially viable and aligned with local urban development plans. By clearly outlining procedures, approval pathways and stakeholder responsibiliƟes, the document provides greater certainty and ease of parƟcipaƟon for private developers, encouraging wider and more conﬁdent engagement in the AHP verƟcal. At the same Ɵme, it simpliﬁes coordinaƟon for States and Urban Local Bodies, reducing procedural boƩlenecks and expediƟng decision-making. I encourage all stakeholders to proacƟvely operaƟonalise these provisions and unlock the full potenƟal of the AHP verƟcal in creaƟng sustainable housing assets for urban beneﬁciaries. Preamble The Government of India accords high priority to the provision of safe, aﬀordable, inclusive and sustainable housing for all urban households. In furtherance of the naƟonal commitment to Housing for All, the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) has been launched w.e.f. 1st September 2024 with an aim to provide all-weather pucca houses with basic civic ameniƟes to eligible beneﬁciaries belonging to the EWS, LIG and MIG categories in urban areas. Under PMAY-U 2.0, the Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal consƟtutes an important supply-side intervenƟon aimed at enhancing the availability of aﬀordable housing through the collaboraƟve parƟcipaƟon of States/UTs, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and public and private sector agencies. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Aﬀairs (MoHUA) has prepared a Standard OperaƟng Procedure (SoP) which aims to guide Public/Private Agencies in eﬀecƟve planning, implementaƟon and monitoring of AHP projects under PMAY-U 2.0 in a structured, transparent and outcome-oriented manner. The key objecƟves of this SoP are to: 1 To provide clear and comprehensive policy guidance to Public and Private Agencies for the systemaƟc planning, appraisal, approval and implementaƟon of the Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal under PMAY-U 2.0; 2 To encourage and facilitate proacƟve parƟcipaƟon of both public and private sector stakeholders in the delivery of aﬀordable housing, leveraging their respecƟve strengths and resources; 3 To promote high standards of construcƟon quality, adherence to prescribed Ɵmelines and achievement of full occupancy of housing projects, thereby ensuring durability and eﬀecƟve uƟlizaƟon of created assets; 4 To promote convergence with other Central, State and local government schemes and programmes in order to enhance overall liveability through improved access to infrastructure, basic services and social ameniƟes; 5 To strengthen insƟtuƟonal and governance mechanisms for eﬀecƟve monitoring, transparency, accountability and beneﬁciary-centric implementaƟon of AHP projects; 6 To support post-compleƟon processes by providing clear and uniform provisions for project handover, allotment, occupancy, and long-term operaƟon and maintenance of housing assets. This SoP lays down a structured framework for the planning, approval, and implementaƟon of AHP projects under PMAY-U 2.0, clearly deﬁning roles, responsibiliƟes and processes from project concepƟon to

accountability and beneﬁciary-centric implementaƟon of AHP projects; 6 To support post-compleƟon processes by providing clear and uniform provisions for project handover, allotment, occupancy, and long-term operaƟon and maintenance of housing assets. This SoP lays down a structured framework for the planning, approval, and implementaƟon of AHP projects under PMAY-U 2.0, clearly deﬁning roles, responsibiliƟes and processes from project concepƟon to handover. It ensures accountability, quality, and Ɵmely delivery through robust beneﬁciary veriﬁcaƟon, DPR appraisal, geo-tagging, quality monitoring and statutory compliance mechanisms. Overall, it facilitates the objecƟve of Housing for All by promoƟng safe, sustainable, and inclusive housing for EWS households through cooperaƟve federalism and public–private collaboraƟon.

Background 1.1 Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-Urban 2.0) is one of the major ﬂagship programs being implemented by Government of India to provide all weather pucca houses to eligible beneﬁciaries in the urban areas across the country. PMAY-U 2.0 has been launched with eﬀect from 1st September 2024 to provide ﬁnancial assistance to urban poor and middle-class families belonging to the Economically Weaker SecƟon (EWS)/ Low Income Group (LIG)/ Middle Income Group (MIG) categories through States/Union Territories (UTs)/Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) to construct, purchase or rent a house at an aﬀordable cost in urban areas over a period of ﬁve years. 1.2 Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-Urban 2.0) is one of the major ﬂagship programs being implemented by Government of India to provide all weather pucca houses to eligible beneﬁciaries in the urban areas across the country. PMAY-U 2.0 has been launched with eﬀect from 1st September 2024 to provide ﬁnancial assistance to urban poor and middle-class families belonging to the Economically Weaker SecƟon (EWS)/ Low Income Group (LIG)/ Middle Income Group (MIG) categories through States/Union Territories (UTs)/Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) to construct, purchase or rent a house at an aﬀordable cost in urban areas over a period of ﬁve years. 1.3 AHP verƟcal of PMAY-U 2.0 supports houses with a minimum carpet area of 30 sqm. Public/Private Agencies will have the ﬂexibility in terms of determining the size of houses up to 45 sqm and other faciliƟes without any enhancement in ﬁnancial assistance from Government of India. Projects must include basic civic ameniƟes (water, sanitaƟon, sewerage, roads, electricity), while States/UTs are responsible for providing trunk infrastructure up to the project site from their own resources. 2. Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership 2.1 The Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal of PMAY-U 2.0 provides Central Assistance to EWS beneﬁciaries for ownership of pucca houses constructed through partnerships involving States/UTs, ULBs and public or private agencies. 2.2 To enhance the supply of aﬀordable housing, AHP projects may be implemented either through government agencies or in partnership with private agencies, including industries. Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verƟcal of PMAY-U 2.0 provides Central Assistance to EWS beneﬁciaries for ownership of pucca houses constructed through partnerships involving States/UTs, ULBs and public or private agencies. 2.2 To enhance the supply of aﬀordable housing, AHP projects may be implemented either through government agencies or in partnership with private agencies, including industries. The projects under AHP are a supply-side intervenƟon under which aﬀordable houses with a carpet area of 30-45 sqm are constructed with basic civic services and social infrastructure by public or private agencies. These houses are alloƩed to eligible EWS beneﬁciaries through a transparent process by the State/UT Governments. 2.3 The AHP verƟcal under PMAY-U 2.0 is implemented through two models: i Model-1: ConstrucƟon of houses by Public Sector agencies and parastatals a Under this model, Public Agencies/Parastatals undertake construcƟon of AHP projects on encumbrance-free land supported by valid ownership documents. b Preliminary Project Report (PPR) covering housing, locaƟon, approx. price, Ɵmeline, layout plans etc. for such AHP projects are to be prepared and publicised on Uniﬁed Web Portal (UWP). c Based on the PPR, the prospecƟve beneﬁciaries may be able to choose preferred AHP project and apply through the UWP as per the process. d The Detailed Project Report (DPR) of such projects are prepared by States/UTs/ULBs covering housing components, infrastructure, ﬁnancial structuring, implementaƟon Ɵmelines and insƟtuƟonal responsibiliƟes and the same shall be uploaded on the UWP. e The DPRs are approved by State Level SancƟoning and Monitoring CommiƩee (SLSMC) of the States/UTs before forwarding to Central SancƟoning and Monitoring CommiƩee (CSMC) for consideraƟon of release of Central Assistance. The AHP Projects must comply with the NaƟonal Building Code (NBC), relevant Indian Standards (IS) and disaster-resilience norms. f States/UTs may also undertake In-situ slum redevelopment, redevelopment of dilapidated housing and reseƩlement of untenable slums under this Model in accordance with PMAY-U 2.0 guidelines, including mandatory de-noƟﬁcaƟon of slums, where applicable. g Central Assistance are released in instalments linked to physical progress, subject to compliance with scheme guidelines and provision of the matching State/UT share. h Flowchart depicƟng steps in AHP (public projects) component

Step by step process for States/UTs/ULBs/Public/Private Agencies for implementation of AHP projects States/UTs/ULBs/ Public/Private Agencies are advised to follow a structured and sequenƟal process for formulaƟon and implementaƟon of Aﬀordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) projects under PMAY-U 2.0, to ensure inclusive, safe and aﬀordable housing for EWS households as under: 5.1 Pre-Approval stage: The following steps shall be followed by Public/Private Agency for the pre-approval stage of AHP projects under PMAY-U 2.0: i Project planning and feasibility analysis: a) Assess housing demand; verify applicaƟons; idenƟfy eligible target beneﬁciaries; and evaluate site condiƟons, land availability and compliance with PMAY-U 2.0 guidelines. b) Examine technical, ﬁnancial and legal feasibility, including cost esƟmates, funding structure, implementaƟon capacity and risk assessment, to ensure Ɵmely, sustainable and cost-eﬀecƟve project execuƟon. c) PrioriƟze AHP projects in Transit Oriented Development (TOD) locaƟons such as areas near metro staƟons, bus/railway terminals, ring roads and major commercial or insƟtuƟonal hubs by adopƟng TOD and precinct-based planning to integrate aﬀordable housing with mass transit, promote mixed- use development, improve access to employment and services for EWS/LIG households and reduce commuƟng costs. d) Plan AHP projects in convergence with other urban missions and State Government schemes (e.g., AMRUT, SBM-U) to ensure adequate infrastructure and civic services, opƟmize resource uƟlizaƟon, avoid duplicaƟon and enhance sustainability and quality of life for beneﬁciaries. e) State/UT Governments shall undertake comprehensive planning for AHP projects based on realisƟc assessments of housing demand, availability of eligible beneﬁciaries, encumbrance-free land and ﬁnancial viability, including project costs, funding sources and long-term sustainability, to ensure Ɵmely compleƟon and eﬀecƟve achievement of the objecƟve of Housing for All. ii. Use of InnovaƟve Technologies in AHP Projects a) States/UTs/ULBs/ImplemenƟng Agencies shall promote the use of innovaƟve, cost-eﬀecƟve, Ɵme- eﬃcient and sustainable construcƟon technologies in AHP projects, in compliance with BIS/NBC standards. b) Such technologies shall aim to reduce construcƟon Ɵme and cost, improve quality and durability, enhance safety and minimize environmental impact. c) Proposals adopƟng innovaƟve technologies shall be assessed during DPR appraisal for technical feasibility, lifecycle cost, local adaptability and maintenance requirements. d) Capacity building may be undertaken to ensure eﬀecƟve implementaƟon. iv PreparaƟon of layout and building plans: a) The implemenƟng agencies shall Prepare detailed site layouts and architectural plans in compliance with local development regulaƟons, PMAY-U 2.0 guidelines and statutory norms. b) The plans may include dwelling units, internal roads, open spaces, parking and civic/social infrastructure. c) The plans shall be submiƩed to statutory authoriƟes (Town Planning, ULB, Fire Department, etc.) for approval. v PreparaƟon of structural design and safety compliance: a) Structural designs of the housing units with basic and social infrastructure faciliƟes shall be developed in accordance with IS/NBC codes and State/Local norms. Due consideraƟons shall be given to factors such as load calculaƟons, soil condiƟons, seismic safety, wind forces and durability requirements etc. b) Designs shall ensure safety, resilience, durability and constructability based on soil, seismic, wind and load consideraƟons etc. vi Project Financial Planning: a) PreparaƟon of detailed cost esƟmates covering construcƟon, land development, infrastructure, statutory approvals and conƟngencies. b) Deﬁne funding paƩern of Central Assistance, State/ULB share and beneﬁciary contribuƟon. c) Under Model-2, Private developers shall arrange private or insƟtuƟonal ﬁnancing for the project.
